The photo template uses "photo": "photos/your-image.jpg". If a date has no entry, a post from 'evergreen' is used instead (rotating by day). Caption placeholders: {brand}, {handle}, {website}, {date}, {weekday}.

2026-11-21.title: Every diamond has a story
2026-11-21.text: We make sure it's the true one. Diamond certification and professional grading courses.
2026-11-21.caption: Welcome to {brand}! We certify diamonds and train the next generation of diamond graders. Follow for a daily dose of diamond knowledge.
2026-11-21.image_idea: A single brilliant diamond lit dramatically on deep navy, with icy blue light.

2026-11-22.label: DID YOU KNOW?
2026-11-22.title: Older than the dinosaurs
2026-11-22.text: Most natural diamonds formed 150+ km below the surface, over a billion years ago.
2026-11-22.caption: The diamond in a ring may be over a billion years old. Every one has a journey worth verifying.
2026-11-22.image_idea: Dramatic cross-section of the Earth with a glowing rough diamond deep inside.

2026-11-23.label: MYTH vs FACT
2026-11-23.title: "It passed the tester, so it's real"
2026-11-23.text: Fact: moissanite can fool a basic thermal tester. Only proper gemmological testing confirms a diamond.
2026-11-23.caption: Pocket testers are a first check, not proof. Moissanite conducts heat like diamond and can read as 'diamond' on basic thermal testers. When it matters, get it certified.
2026-11-23.image_idea: Split image: a diamond and a look-alike stone side by side, with a red 'MYTH' and green 'FACT' feel.

2026-11-24.label: GRADING 101
2026-11-24.title: The 4Cs in one minute
2026-11-24.text: Cut, Colour, Clarity and Carat: the four factors every grader assesses.
2026-11-24.caption: Cut, Colour, Clarity and Carat - the universal language of diamond quality. Over the next weeks we'll break each one down. Save this post!
2026-11-24.image_idea: Four elegant tiles, each with a diamond close-up for cut, colour, clarity and carat.

2026-11-25.label: INSIDE THE LAB
2026-11-25.title: A diamond's journey at IGCC
2026-11-25.text: Received. Inspected. Measured. Graded. Reported. Every stone, step by step.
2026-11-25.caption: What happens after you hand us a diamond? Every stone goes through careful inspection, measurement and grading before a report is issued.
2026-11-25.image_idea: Gemmologist's gloved hands placing a diamond under a microscope in a clean modern lab.

2026-11-26.label: QUIZ TIME
2026-11-26.title: Which C measures weight?
2026-11-26.text:
A) Cut   B) Carat   C) Clarity
Comment your answer!
2026-11-26.caption: Quick quiz! Which of the 4Cs measures weight, not size? Comment A, B or C - answer in tomorrow's story.
2026-11-26.image_idea: Diamond on a precision scale, with bold quiz layout and A/B/C options.

2026-11-27.title: Learn to grade like a professional
2026-11-27.text: Hands-on diamond grading training from a working certification lab.
2026-11-27.caption: Want to turn your love for diamonds into a skill? Our diamond grading course teaches you to assess stones the way a lab does. DM us for the next batch.
2026-11-27.image_idea: Students in a modern classroom examining diamonds with loupes, warm and aspirational.

2026-11-28.label: BUYER'S GUIDE
2026-11-28.title: 5 things to check on a diamond report
2026-11-28.text: Report number - Laser inscription - The 4Cs - Measurements - Treatment disclosure
2026-11-28.caption: Before you buy, read the report: 1) report number 2) laser inscription 3) the 4Cs 4) measurements 5) any treatment disclosure. Save this for your next purchase.
2026-11-28.image_idea: A diamond grading report on a desk next to a loose diamond and tweezers.

2026-11-29.label: THE SCIENCE OF SPARKLE
2026-11-29.title: Why diamonds sparkle
2026-11-29.text: Brilliance is white light returned to your eye. Fire is light split into rainbow colours.
2026-11-29.caption: Brilliance, fire and scintillation - three ways a diamond plays with light. A great cut is what unlocks them.
2026-11-29.image_idea: Macro shot of a diamond throwing rainbow flashes of light on a dark background.

2026-11-30.label: MYTH vs FACT
2026-11-30.title: "Lab-grown diamonds are fake"
2026-11-30.text: Fact: lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds. The difference is origin, and it must be disclosed.
2026-11-30.caption: Lab-grown diamonds are carbon crystals just like natural ones. What matters is honest disclosure - and that's exactly what a lab report gives you.
2026-11-30.image_idea: Two identical diamonds side by side, one labelled 'natural', one 'lab-grown'.

2026-12-01.label: GRADING 101 - COLOUR
2026-12-01.title: From D to Z
2026-12-01.text: Colourless diamonds are graded D (colourless) to Z (light yellow or brown). The closer to D, the rarer.
2026-12-01.caption: Colour is about the absence of colour. Differences between grades can be invisible to the untrained eye - that's why graders compare against master stones.
2026-12-01.image_idea: A row of diamonds showing a subtle colourless-to-yellow gradient on white.

2026-12-02.label: INSIDE THE LAB
2026-12-02.title: Natural or lab-grown?
2026-12-02.text: They can look identical. Advanced instruments reveal how a diamond grew.
2026-12-02.caption: Even experts can't tell natural from lab-grown by eye. Labs use specialised instruments to read the growth story inside the stone.
2026-12-02.image_idea: Diamond inside a high-tech testing instrument with soft blue light.

2026-12-03.label: SPOT THE DIFFERENCE
2026-12-03.title: Natural or lab-grown?
2026-12-03.text:
Left or right - which one is natural?
Comment your guess!
2026-12-03.caption: Can you spot the natural diamond? Trick question - you can't by eye. That's why certification matters. Comment your guess anyway!
2026-12-03.image_idea: Two identical-looking diamonds side by side labelled LEFT and RIGHT.

2026-12-04.title: Where diamond grading can take you
2026-12-04.text: Diamond grader - Jewellery buyer - Retail consultant - Quality control - Your own business
2026-12-04.caption: A grading qualification opens doors across the diamond and jewellery trade. Which career would you choose? DM us to start your journey.
2026-12-04.image_idea: Confident young professional with a loupe in an elegant jewellery store.

2026-12-05.label: WEDDING SEASON
2026-12-05.title: Buying a diamond this season?
2026-12-05.text: Insist on a report. Match the stone to it. Ask about treatments. Buy with confidence.
2026-12-05.caption: Wedding season is here! Before you buy that special piece, make sure the diamond is certified and the report matches the stone.
2026-12-05.image_idea: Elegant Indian bridal jewellery with a diamond ring in focus, rich but tasteful.

2026-12-06.label: DID YOU KNOW?
2026-12-06.title: Diamonds come in every colour
2026-12-06.text: Traces of boron make diamonds blue. Nitrogen makes them yellow.
2026-12-06.caption: Pink, blue, yellow, green - coloured diamonds owe their hues to tiny traces of other elements or structural changes. Some are among the rarest gems on Earth.
2026-12-06.image_idea: A rainbow arrangement of fancy coloured diamonds on dark velvet.

2026-12-07.label: MYTH vs FACT
2026-12-07.title: "Diamonds can't break"
2026-12-07.text: Fact: diamond is the hardest natural material, but a hard knock can still chip it.
2026-12-07.caption: Hard is not the same as unbreakable. Diamonds can chip along their cleavage planes with a sharp blow, so treat them with care.
2026-12-07.image_idea: Diamond ring on a hard stone surface with dramatic lighting.

2026-12-08.label: GRADING 101 - CLARITY
2026-12-08.title: FL to I3: 11 clarity grades
2026-12-08.text: Clarity describes the size, number and position of inclusions and blemishes.
2026-12-08.caption: Most inclusions are only visible under 10x magnification - nature's fingerprints that make each diamond unique, and help identify it.
2026-12-08.image_idea: Extreme macro of a diamond interior showing a tiny natural inclusion.

2026-12-09.label: TOOLS OF THE TRADE
2026-12-09.title: A gemmologist's toolkit
2026-12-09.text: 10x loupe - Tweezers - Microscope - Master stones - Precision scale
2026-12-09.caption: Every grade starts with the right tools and a trained eye. Learn to use them in our grading course.
2026-12-09.image_idea: Flat-lay of gemmology tools on navy: loupe, tweezers, scale, diamond.

2026-12-10.label: QUIZ TIME
2026-12-10.title: How many facets on a round brilliant?
2026-12-10.text:
A) 33   B) 57 or 58   C) 72
Comment your answer!
2026-12-10.caption: Count the facets! How many does a standard round brilliant diamond have? Comment your answer.
2026-12-10.image_idea: Top-down view of a round brilliant diamond showing its facet pattern.

2026-12-11.title: What you'll learn
2026-12-11.text: The 4Cs - Spotting simulants - Lab-grown detection - Reading reports - Hands-on practice
2026-12-11.caption: From the 4Cs to telling diamonds from look-alikes, our course takes you from enthusiast to confident grader. DM us for course details.
2026-12-11.image_idea: Close-up of a student's hand holding a diamond with tweezers under a lamp.

2026-12-12.label: BUYER TIP
2026-12-12.title: Look for the laser inscription
2026-12-12.text: Many certified diamonds carry their report number on the girdle. Check it matches.
2026-12-12.caption: A tiny inscription on the girdle links the stone to its report. Ask your jeweller to show it to you under magnification.
2026-12-12.image_idea: Extreme macro of a diamond girdle with a tiny laser-inscribed number.

2026-12-13.label: DID YOU KNOW?
2026-12-13.title: Carat comes from a seed
2026-12-13.text: Traders once weighed gems against carob seeds. Today one carat is exactly 0.2 grams.
2026-12-13.caption: The word 'carat' traces back to the carob seed, once used as a counterweight. Today it's a precise unit: 1 carat = 0.2 grams.
2026-12-13.image_idea: Carob seeds and a diamond on an antique brass balance scale.

2026-12-14.label: MYTH vs FACT
2026-12-14.title: "Bigger carat always means better"
2026-12-14.text: Fact: cut decides the sparkle. A well-cut smaller diamond can outshine a bigger one.
2026-12-14.caption: Size catches the eye, but cut brings the beauty. Don't judge a diamond by carat alone.
2026-12-14.image_idea: Two diamonds: a smaller one sparkling brilliantly, a larger dull one.

2026-12-15.label: GRADING 101 - CUT
2026-12-15.title: Proportions, symmetry, polish
2026-12-15.text: Cut grading looks at how well a diamond is proportioned and finished - the C that drives sparkle.
2026-12-15.caption: Cut is the only C shaped entirely by human hands. Graders assess proportions, symmetry and polish to judge how well a diamond handles light.
2026-12-15.image_idea: Technical side profile of a diamond with elegant proportion lines.

2026-12-16.label: INSIDE THE LAB
2026-12-16.title: Treatments we look for
2026-12-16.text: Fracture filling - Laser drilling - Colour treatment. Treatments must always be disclosed.
2026-12-16.caption: Some diamonds are treated to improve their look. That's not always bad - but it must be disclosed. Our reports tell you.
2026-12-16.image_idea: Diamond under a microscope with a magnified inset view.

2026-12-17.label: QUIZ TIME
2026-12-17.title: Which one is a diamond simulant?
2026-12-17.text:
A) Moissanite   B) Cubic zirconia   C) Both
Comment your answer!
2026-12-17.caption: Simulants look like diamonds but aren't. Which of these is one? Comment A, B or C!
2026-12-17.image_idea: Three sparkling stones on velvet labelled A, B and C.

2026-12-18.title: Learn from a working lab
2026-12-18.text: Our trainers grade real diamonds every day. Learn the skills the trade actually uses.
2026-12-18.caption: Learn diamond grading where it actually happens - in a certification lab. DM us to join the next batch.
2026-12-18.image_idea: Trainer guiding a student at a microscope in a modern lab.

2026-12-19.label: BUYER TIP
2026-12-19.title: Why certification matters
2026-12-19.text: Resale, insurance, peace of mind. A report from an independent lab protects your investment.
2026-12-19.caption: An independent report makes your diamond easier to insure, resell and trust. Always ask for one.
2026-12-19.image_idea: Diamond ring beside a certificate, warm premium lighting.

2026-12-20.label: DID YOU KNOW?
2026-12-20.title: Some diamonds glow
2026-12-20.text: Under UV light, many diamonds show fluorescence - most often blue.
2026-12-20.caption: Fluorescence is a natural reaction to UV light. Graders record it on the report because it can affect appearance and value.
2026-12-20.image_idea: Diamond glowing blue under ultraviolet light in a dark room.

evergreen.label: BUYER TIP
evergreen.title: Match the report to the stone
evergreen.text: If your diamond has a laser inscription on its girdle, check that the number matches the one on its report.
evergreen.caption: A report only protects you if it belongs to your diamond. Always check the details match.

evergreen.label: DIAMOND CARE
evergreen.title: Keep it sparkling
evergreen.text: Soak in warm water with a little mild soap, then brush gently with a soft toothbrush. Rinse and pat dry.
evergreen.caption: Oils and lotions dull a diamond's sparkle. A simple clean at home brings it back.

evergreen.label: DID YOU KNOW?
evergreen.title: Hard, not unbreakable
evergreen.text: Diamond is the hardest natural material, 10 on the Mohs scale - but a sharp knock can still chip it.
evergreen.caption: Hardness resists scratches, not impacts. Store diamond jewellery separately and take it off for heavy work.

evergreen.label: DID YOU KNOW?
evergreen.title: Some diamonds glow
evergreen.text: Under ultraviolet light, many diamonds show fluorescence - most often blue. It's noted on grading reports.
evergreen.caption: Fluorescence is one of the details a grading report records. Have you ever seen a diamond glow?

evergreen.label: LOOK-ALIKES
evergreen.title: Not everything that sparkles is diamond
evergreen.text: Cubic zirconia and moissanite can look similar at a glance. Proper gemmological testing tells them apart.
evergreen.caption: Simulants are common in the market. When in doubt, get it tested.

evergreen.text: Confidence comes from knowing exactly what you own.
